headline: Up to $22,000 approved for mausoleum roof repair work
summary: A contractor quoted $17,975 for the lower-priority areas, which is more than the money set aside. Other companies had not yet provided quotes, and the contractor did not price winter work. Spending from the perpetual care account also needs city council approval.
decisions: Approved up to $22,000 from the perpetual care interest account for mausoleum roof repairs.
discussion: Mausoleum roof repair: Members weighed a contractor's quote for work in phases, with high-priority areas first. Some favored waiting until spring to avoid winter costs, while others favored starting before the weather turned cold.
Expansion proposals: Staff plans to send a request for proposals to four on-call companies that showed interest, within about a week. Responses usually take two to four weeks.

Cremation burial area: Staff reported more families were choosing direct cremation, which takes more staff time. Members discussed a possible cremation-only section with upright markers, with the layout still to be drawn by an engineer.
Mowing slope safety: Staff said most mowers are rated for slopes up to 20 degrees, and one ride-on mower up to 15 degrees. Staff will look into robotic mowers and ground covers for slopes.

Sewer project funding: Staff said the city must separate its combined sewers by 2030 under a consent decree. Principal forgiveness on state loans shortens repayment but does not reduce the amount borrowed.

decision_evidence.quote: So I'll ask for a motion to permit the expenditure of up to $22,000 from the perpetual care interest account to cover the work necessary to re-point the Muslim rules. Make a motion. Second. All in favor? Aye. Any opposed? Passes.

decision_titles: Up to $22,000 from perpetual care interest account
